intro: How a utility tells smart inverters, batteries and chargers what to do, over the internet. The device is the client: it fetches XML resources from the utility's server over HTTPS, follows the links in them, and posts back its responses and readings. A certificate on each side proves who is talking.

tls.title: Show certificates
tls.text: The inverter opens a TLS 1.2 connection to the utility's server. Both sides show a certificate, and only one cipher suite is allowed. Now each side knows who the other is.

discover.title: Find itself
discover.text: The inverter knows one address: /dcap. From there it follows links to the list of end devices, and finds the one whose lFDI matches its own certificate.

control.title: Get the control
control.text: Through its program, the inverter reads a DERControl: limit output to 50 % for two hours, from 11:00 UTC.

received.title: Confirm receipt
received.text: The control asks for responses. The inverter posts one: status 1, received.

start.title: Limit output
start.text: At 11:00, by its own clock, the inverter cuts its output from 9.6 kW to 5.0 kW (50 % of its 10 kW) and posts status 2, started.

report.title: Report the output
report.text: The inverter posts its measured power into its mirror on the server. The utility sees that the limit is kept.

frames.client-hello: Hello. I speak TLS 1.2, with this one cipher suite
frames.server-hello: Agreed. Here is my certificate. Show me yours
frames.client-finished: Here is my certificate, and proof that I hold its key
frames.server-finished: Your certificate checks out. From now on, we are encrypted
frames.dcap: My lists: end devices, mirrors, time and more
frames.get-edev: Which end devices do you know?
frames.get-derc: Which controls are there for me?
frames.post-reading: My active power is now 5000 W

notes.server-hello: Four messages in one flight. ServerHello picks 0xC0AE. Certificate carries the server's certificate chain. ServerKeyExchange carries its half of the ECDHE key agreement. CertificateRequest asks for the client's certificate: without it, TLS would check only the server.
notes.client-finished: The inverter sends its device certificate and its half of the key agreement. Then it signs the whole handshake with its private key (CertificateVerify): only the real owner of the certificate can do that. The certificate was put in at the factory, under the IEEE 2030.5 PKI, and it never expires.
notes.server-finished: The server checks the inverter's certificate chain up to the root it trusts, then sends its own Finished. From here on, every record is encrypted. HTTP travels inside, and nobody on the way can read or change it.
notes.get-dcap: Inside TLS: GET /dcap HTTP/1.1, with Accept: application/sep+xml. /dcap is the one address a client is given. It finds every other address through links.
notes.dcap: A DeviceCapability resource: links such as EndDeviceListLink href="/edev", MirrorUsagePointListLink href="/mup" and TimeLink href="/tm". pollRate="900": poll these resources every 900 s.
notes.get-edev: The list of end devices. The server may list only the devices this certificate is allowed to see.
notes.edev: Each EndDevice holds an lFDI and an sFDI. /edev/3 holds BB1309569EF761C13E620EA80AA3E84D2B6B553D, the inverter's own. The installer gave its SFDI to the utility when the inverter was installed.
notes.get-derc: Before this, two more GETs like it: from /edev/3 to its FunctionSetAssignments, then to the list of DER programs. Program /derp/1 links to its controls.
notes.derc: One DERControl, shown line by line in the playground: opModMaxLimW 5000 (50.00 %) for 7200 s, from 1781694000 (11:00 UTC).
notes.post-received: A DERControlResponse, posted to the control's replyTo address. It holds the inverter's lFDI, the control's mRID as its subject, and status 1: received.
notes.created: HTTP 201 Created. The Location header gives the address of the stored response.
notes.post-started: The same response with status 2: started. At 13:00 the inverter will post status 3, completed, and go back to its default control.
notes.post-reading: A MirrorMeterReading. The server keeps a mirror of the inverter's meter (a MirrorUsagePoint), and the inverter fills it. Its ReadingType gives the unit: uom 38 means watts.

client-version.name: Client version
client-version.note: The highest version the inverter speaks: TLS 1.2.

random.name: Random
random.note: 32 random bytes. Both sides mix them into the session keys.

session-id.name: Session ID
session-id.note: Length 0: no earlier session to resume.

suites-length.name: Cipher suites
suites-length.note: 2 bytes of cipher suites follow: just one.

suite.name: 0xC0AE
suite.note: TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CCM_8, the suite IEEE 2030.5 requires. ECDHE agrees the keys, ECDSA signs the certificates, and AES-128 in CCM mode encrypts the data, with an 8-byte tag.

groups.name: supported_groups
groups.note: Extension 0x000A: only secp256r1 (0x0017), the P-256 curve.

point-formats.name: ec_point_formats
point-formats.note: Extension 0x000B: curve points are sent uncompressed (0).

a-first36.name: First 36 bits
a-first36.note: The first 9 hex digits. They make the SFDI.

a-rest.name: Rest of the LFDI
a-rest.note: With the first 9 digits, the first 20 bytes (40 hex digits) of the fingerprint: the LFDI.

a-dropped.name: Not used
a-dropped.note: The last 12 bytes of the SHA-256 fingerprint are dropped.

s-check.name: Check digit
s-check.note: It makes the sum of all digits a multiple of 10: 5+0+2+1+7+3+9+1+4+6+5 = 43, and 43 + 7 = 50. A typing mistake breaks the sum.

facts.between: Utility or aggregator server → inverters, batteries, EV chargers
facts.security: TLS 1.2 with 0xC0AE, a certificate on each side
facts.model: Resources linked by URLs: DeviceCapability → EndDevice → DERProgram → DERControl

tips: The LFDI comes from the certificate. A new certificate means a new LFDI and SFDI, and the device must be registered again.
Controls use Unix time in UTC. An inverter with a wrong clock limits at the wrong time, so keep it in step with the server's Time resource (/tm).
Start from /dcap and follow the links every time. Every other address belongs to the server and can change.
Most inverters sit behind a router that blocks incoming connections, so they poll. Poll at pollRate, not faster: thousands of devices share one server.

anatomy.lfdi: The LFDI: the first 20 bytes of the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint
anatomy.sfdi: The SFDI: a short form a person can type

playground.file: The DERControl the inverter reads in step 3. Pick a marked line to see what it means.
playground.href: The control's own address. The namespace urn:ieee:std:2030.5:ns marks every IEEE 2030.5 document.
playground.reply: Where to post responses (replyTo), and which ones: responseRequired 03 asks for received, then started and completed.
playground.mrid: A 128-bit ID, unique worldwide; responses name it. Its last 8 hex digits are the issuer's IANA enterprise number: 32473 (0x7ED9) is the one kept for examples.
playground.created: Times are Unix seconds in UTC: 1781686800 is 2026-06-17 09:00.
playground.start: 1781694000: 11:00 UTC. The inverter waits for it by its own clock.
playground.limit: Maximum output, in hundredths of a percent of the inverter's set maximum power (setMaxW): 5000 = 50.00 %.
